title: HuBMAP: Embedding Fixed Frozen OCT Samples
author: Marda Jorgensen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.basniede
materials: Prepare 1x PBS PBS is required to prepare reagents needed for this procedure. Dilute 10x PBS 1:10 in deionized water to make working 1x solution. PBS Phosphate Buffered Saline 10X Solution Fisher BioReagents Fisher Scientific Catalog #BP399-1

steps.title: Prepare 4% paraformaldehyde fixative
steps.instruction: Wear gloves, lab coat and work in a fume hood. Add 60 mL of 100 mM PBS to a sample cup, then open two 10 mL ampules of 16 % paraformaldehyde stock (total 20 mL) and add to the PBS. Invert the cup to mix, yielding a 4 % paraformaldehyde solution in PBS. Prepare enough containers so that the tissue‑to‑fixative volume ratio is at least 1:20.

steps.title: Prepare 30% sucrose solution
steps.instruction: Combine 300 g sucrose with 1 L 1× PBS in a labeled container, add a stir bar and mix on a stir plate until fully dissolved. Label the container; the solution expires one week after preparation and should be stored at 4 °C if not used immediately.

steps.title: Prepare 15% sucrose solution
steps.instruction: Mix equal volumes of the freshly made 30 % sucrose solution and 1× PBS to obtain a 15 % sucrose solution. Store the mixture at 4 °C for at least 8 hours before use.

steps.title: Collect and cassette tissue specimens
steps.instruction: Collect tissue specimens from the designated common coordinate framework sites (see SOP Appendices for spleen, thymus, lymph node). Place each specimen into a pre‑labelled cassette, preserving its anatomical orientation.

steps.title: Fix tissue in 4% PFA
steps.instruction: Transfer each cassette‑contained tissue into a 120 mL specimen container that already contains 80 mL of the freshly prepared 4 % paraformaldehyde fixative. Fix the tissue for 24 hours at room temperature on a rocker (mild agitation).

steps.title: Wash tissue post‑fixation
steps.instruction: Drain the used fixative (collect as hazardous waste). Wash the tissue three times, each wash lasting 10 minutes, in 1× PBS that generously covers the specimen. During each wash invert the container several times or return it to the rocker.

steps.title: Cryoprotect tissue with sucrose
steps.instruction: Replace the final PBS wash with the 15 % sucrose solution and incubate the tissue at 4 °C for 8 hours. Then replace the 15 % sucrose with the 30 % sucrose solution and equilibrate the tissue at 4 °C for at least 48 hours (up to 72 hours). Tissue remains stable in 30 % sucrose for at least one week.

steps.title: Prepare pre‑labeled Cryomold with OCT
steps.instruction: Label a Cryomold® (Histology, Tissue‑Tek®, 25 mm × 20 mm × 5 mm, catalog #25608‑916). Fill the mold halfway with Tissue‑Tek® O.C.T. Compound (catalog #25608‑930).

steps.title: Transfer tissue to Cryomold
steps.instruction: Using forceps, remove the tissue from its cassette, quickly dab the surface with a Kimwipe to remove excess sucrose droplets, and place the tissue into the OCT‑filled Cryomold, maintaining the original orientation.

steps.title: Add OCT and equilibrate
steps.instruction: Gently push the tissue to the bottom of the Cryomold with forceps, then add additional OCT to completely cover the tissue and fill the mold. Allow the block to equilibrate in the mold for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare dry ice/methylbutane slurry
steps.instruction: Place 1–2 inches of dry‑ice pellets into the bottom of an ice bucket or styrofoam box. Add enough 2‑methylbutane to cover the dry ice by ~5 mm. Close the lid and let the chamber chill until fog dissipates and the bucket bottom becomes visible, indicating the slurry is ready.

steps.title: Freeze tissue block in Cryomold
steps.instruction: Rest the Cryomold on the surface of the chilled methylbutane slurry. As the OCT begins to freeze, gently push the tissue to the bottom of the mold one final time. Continue until the Cryomold is completely frozen and opaque.

steps.title: Wrap and store frozen block
steps.instruction: Wrap the frozen Cryomold in a pre‑labeled aluminum‑foil square, place it in a freezer rack box, and store at –80 °C. Record the block location in the Freezer Log for future retrieval.
